title: Under the Hood
author: Claude
blurb: Three short levels about what the player program is made of. Level 1 walks along a row of bytes and picks up the four at offset 2575B that spell Play. Level 2 tries two words in a four-byte slot: START does not fit, GO and two spaces does. Level 3 is about asking first: make a backup copy, change only your own copy, and leave the credits alone. None of the levels changes a real player; the signs only show the ideas. Play it, then read the Programmer's Guide chapter on patching the player.

box.tagline: A program is a row of bytes.
box.back: A small explorer in a blue beanie walks through a player program, one byte at a time. Pick up the four bytes that spell Play, try two words in a four-byte slot, and learn what to ask before changing anything. Read the signs, then read the Programmer's Guide chapter on patching the player.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Real offsets and sizes from the DOS player
Made to be copied and taken apart
